name: Agra
tagline: The Mughal city forever crowned by the Taj Mahal.
bestMonths: Jan, Feb, Mar, Oct, Nov and Dec
whenBlurb: Visit October to March for cool, clear days at the Taj, with February's Taj Mahotsav the cultural high point; escape the April to June furnace and the July to September monsoon haze.

ourTake.lede: Agra is a one-night city that most people treat as a half-day, and that is the mistake; stay over so you can be at the Taj Mahal at sunrise and again see it change colour, rather than fighting the midday crowds. Don't neglect Agra Fort and the often-empty 'Baby Taj', and consider Fatehpur Sikri on the way in or out. Choose a hotel with a Taj view; you will thank yourself at dawn.
ourTake.comeIf: You want the Taj at dawn and a night in a view-facing suite.
ourTake.skipIf: You want more than a day or two, Agra is a single, perfect stop.

guide.lede: Where to stay, what to do, where to eat, and where the night goes, grouped by price, every address earned by a name worth trusting.

items.name: The Oberoi Amarvilas
items.area: Taj Ganj (600m from the Taj Mahal)
credentials: Condé Nast Traveler Readers' Choice, top-ranked Agra hotel (historic)
Only luxury hotel in Agra with unrestricted Taj views from all rooms & suites
items.description: The only hotel on earth with unrestricted Taj Mahal views from every room, Agra's undisputed icon.

items.name: ITC Mughal, a Luxury Collection Resort & Spa
credentials: LEED Platinum (also LEED Zero Carbon & Zero Water) certified
Kaya Kalp – The Royal Spa, Tatler & Condé Nast recognised spa
items.description: A Mughal-scale resort on 35 acres, the only Indian hotel to win the Aga Khan Award for Architecture, and a landmark spa.

items.name: Taj Hotel & Convention Centre, Agra
items.area: Taj Ganj (walking distance from the Taj Mahal)
credentials: One of North India's largest pillar-less banquet halls (14,000 sq ft)
items.description: IHCL's Taj brand in Agra, contemporary grandeur and one of North India's largest pillar-less halls, minutes from the monument.

items.name: Trident Agra
credentials: The Oberoi Group, Trident (EIH Associated Hotels)
items.description: The Oberoi Group's polished, garden-set house, a quietly reliable Agra address a short drive from the Taj.

items.name: DoubleTree by Hilton Agra
credentials: Rooms & pool with Taj Mahal views (~2km from the monument)
items.description: A modern Hilton with genuine Taj Mahal views, one of the few in the city to offer them off the monument.

items.name: Courtyard by Marriott Agra
items.description: A dependable Marriott a couple of kilometres from the Taj, modern, easy and well-located for the monuments.

items.name: Radisson Hotel Agra
items.description: A full-service riverside house with Taj views, a rooftop terrace and its own art gallery.

items.name: The Taj Mahal at Sunrise
items.description: Enter as the gates open and the marble shifts from grey to blush to blinding white before the crowds arrive, the light no photograph has ever caught. From Oberoi Amarvilas or ITC Mughal a car has you at the West Gate first in line, and the whole monument is meat-free ground, so a Jain or vegetarian family reaches it fasting and untroubled.

items.name: Taj Mahal Moonlight Viewing (full-moon nights)
items.description: For five nights a month, the full moon and two on either side, a limited number of visitors enter after dark in batches of fifty to see the marble glow silver under the moon. It is the most romantic and most exclusive way to meet the Taj; the concierge can secure the ballot slot and the timing that suits a multi-generational party.

items.name: The Taj from Mehtab Bagh (across the Yamuna)
items.description: The 'Moonlight Garden' Babur laid out directly opposite frames the Taj perfectly reflected in the river at sunset, with almost no crowd and no queue. Photographers call it the finest view of all; it is the quiet counterpoint to the sunrise rush, and where Shah Jahan reputedly planned his own black-marble mausoleum.

items.name: Agra Fort
items.description: The red-sandstone imperial city where Shah Jahan was imprisoned by his son and spent his last years gazing at the Taj he built for Mumtaz, the whole Mughal romance in one walled fortress. The marble palaces, the Diwan-i-Khas and the Musamman Burj tower reward a private guide who knows the family drama behind each courtyard.

items.name: Itmad-ud-Daulah's Tomb (the 'Baby Taj')
items.description: Nur Jahan's exquisite tomb for her father was the first Mughal building faced entirely in white marble and the first to use pietra-dura inlay, the aesthetic rehearsal for the Taj itself. It is small, jewel-like and blissfully uncrowded, best appreciated slowly with someone who can read the inlaid flowers.

items.name: Akbar's Tomb, Sikandra
items.description: The great emperor Akbar planned his own resting place, and its five-tiered gateway and blend of Islamic, Hindu, Jain and Christian motifs embody his ideal of a shared faith. Blackbuck and langurs roam the vast char-bagh garden, and the early-morning quiet makes it a serene first or last stop from the city.

items.name: Fatehpur Sikri
items.description: Akbar's perfectly preserved 'ghost capital', abandoned after only fourteen years, holds the towering Buland Darwaza, the Panch Mahal and the Diwan-i-Khas with its extraordinary central pillar. A half-day private excursion with a good historian turns a red-sandstone ruin into the story of Mughal power at its peak.

items.name: The Tomb of Salim Chishti, Fatehpur Sikri
items.description: Inside the Jama Masjid at Fatehpur Sikri, this delicate white-marble shrine to the Sufi saint who blessed Akbar with an heir is wrapped in the finest carved-marble jali screens in India. Pilgrims still tie threads at the lattice; it is intimate, spiritual and quite separate from the imperial grandeur outside.

items.name: Keoladeo National Park, Bharatpur
items.description: One of Asia's great bird sanctuaries, this former royal duck-shoot draws hundreds of resident and migratory species, herons, painted storks, cranes, pelicans, best explored at dawn from a cycle-rickshaw whose driver is a self-taught ornithologist. A gentle, unhurried day that pairs beautifully with Fatehpur Sikri en route.

items.name: Mehtab Bagh Garden
items.description: Beyond the famous river view, the restored Mughal char-bagh itself is a peaceful walled garden of geometric paths, fountains and framed sightlines back to the Taj. Come at golden hour when the light softens and the crowds are all across the water, and the garden is almost your own.

items.name: Chini ka Rauza
items.description: A rare and unrestored jewel, the tomb of a Persian scholar-poet, its facade once entirely sheathed in glazed Persian tilework, the only such building in India. Weathered and little-visited, it rewards the curious traveller who wants Mughal Agra beyond the postcard set.

items.name: Ram Bagh (Aram Bagh)
items.description: Laid out by Babur in 1528, this is considered the earliest surviving Mughal garden in India, the prototype of the paradise char-bagh that culminated in the Taj. Its terraces, water channels and cooling pavilions are a quiet lesson in how the Mughals engineered greenery and breeze against the heat.

items.name: Jama Masjid, Agra
items.description: Shah Jahan's great congregational mosque, built and named for his daughter Jahanara, rises in red sandstone and white-marble inlay right beside the old-city bazaars. Stepping from its calm courtyard straight into the lanes of Kinari Bazaar is one of Agra's best contrasts of the imperial and the everyday.

items.name: Mughal Heritage Walk
items.description: A community-led walk through Kachhpura village on the far bank threads past the Gyarah Sidi (an early Mughal observatory), lesser tombs and everyday village life, ending at a stunning Taj view. It is the antidote to the monument circuit, real, textured and directly supporting the local community.

items.name: Kinari Bazaar & the Old City
items.description: The tangled, canopied lanes behind Jama Masjid are the retail heart of old Agra, zari borders, bangles, brassware, spices and the aroma of frying jalebis. Walk it early with a local guide, then let the concierge arrange a discreet car to collect you at the edge when the crowd gets close.

items.name: Marble Inlay (Pietra Dura) Artisan Workshop
items.description: The descendants of the craftsmen who built the Taj still cut and set jasper, carnelian, malachite and lapis into white marble by hand, one petal at a time. A private studio visit, watching a tabletop take shape and commissioning your own piece, is the finest, most personal souvenir of the marble city.

items.name: Taj Nature Walk
items.description: A landscaped forest reserve minutes from the East Gate, laced with trails, viewing mounds and birdlife, offering clean, framed vistas of the Taj across the greenery. It is a cool, quiet morning stroll and a photographer's favourite for a Taj shot without another soul in the frame.

items.name: Mariam-uz-Zamani's Tomb, Sikandra
items.description: The tomb of Akbar's queen (mother of Jahangir), a short step from Akbar's own mausoleum, is a graceful and almost deserted red-sandstone building. Pairing it with Akbar's Tomb makes an unhurried, crowd-free Sikandra morning for those who like their history quiet.

items.name: Sadar Bazaar
items.description: Agra's cleaner, more relaxed shopping street near the Cantonment is the place for the city's renowned leather, handmade shoes, bags and belts, alongside cafes and sweet shops. An easy, comfortable evening browse when the old city feels too intense.

items.name: Panchhi Petha (the original petha)
items.description: Petha, the translucent ash-gourd sweet, is Agra's edible signature, and Panchhi is its most famous name, offering everything from the plain classic to saffron, paan and dry-fruit versions. A box packed to travel is the traditional gift home; a vegetarian, no-question indulgence.

items.name: Mathura, Krishna Janmabhoomi
items.description: The believed birthplace of Lord Krishna is the spiritual centre of the Braj region and a deeply moving pilgrimage for many Indian families. A guided half-day, ideally around aarti, opens the temple town's rhythm; the concierge can arrange priority darshan and a knowledgeable escort.

items.name: Vrindavan, Banke Bihari Temple
items.description: The most beloved temple of Krishna's childhood town, where the deity's curtain is drawn and closed rhythmically and the crowd surges with devotion, an intense, joyful darshan. Best experienced with a local guide who can time your visit and steer a family through the throng gracefully.

items.name: Prem Mandir, Vrindavan
items.description: A vast modern marble temple set in gardens, illuminated at night in changing colours with musical fountains, spectacular, immaculate and easy for elderly relatives and children alike. It makes a serene, comfortable evening counterpoint to the older, denser temples of Braj.

items.name: ISKCON Vrindavan (Krishna Balaram Mandir)
items.description: The well-run, welcoming Hare Krishna temple offers calm, beautifully kept surroundings, kirtan and pure-vegetarian prasad, an accessible, unhurried introduction to Vrindavan for first-time visitors. A gentle, orderly stop within a Mathura–Vrindavan day.

items.name: Wildlife SOS Agra Bear Rescue Facility
items.description: The world's largest sloth-bear rescue centre, home to bears saved from the cruel 'dancing bear' trade, plus rescued elephants, a genuinely moving, ethical wildlife experience. A meaningful multi-generational morning, especially with children, and directly supportive of conservation.

items.name: Keetham Lake (Sur Sarovar Bird Sanctuary)
items.description: A tranquil lake and wetland reserve on the Delhi road, rich in migratory waterfowl and an easy pairing with the Wildlife SOS centre nearby. A restful, green half-morning away from monuments for those who want birdsong over marble.

items.name: Soami Bagh Samadh, Dayalbagh
items.description: The Radhasoami memorial has been under construction for over a century, its white-marble carving and inlay work said to rival the Taj in ambition and craftsmanship. Rarely on the tourist trail, it is a fascinating stop for anyone drawn to marble artistry and living devotion.

items.name: Mankameshwar Temple
items.description: One of Agra's oldest and most revered Shiva temples, tucked in the old-city lanes near the Jama Masjid, believed to grant the wishes brought to it. A short, atmospheric detour that grounds a heritage walk in the living city rather than its monuments.

items.name: Deeg Palace
items.description: The elegant 18th-century Jat summer palace, with its cooling pavilions, gardens and monsoon fountains, is a lovely and near-empty add-on to a Bharatpur day. A refined, off-radar stop for travellers who have already done the Mughal set and want something rarer.

items.name: Anguri Bagh & the Marble Palaces (within Agra Fort)
items.description: Deep inside the fort, the geometric 'grape garden' fronts the Khas Mahal and the mirrored Sheesh Mahal, the most intimate of the royal apartments. A private guide who can open the finer detail here turns a fort visit into a study of imperial domestic life.

items.name: Diwan-i-Khas & the pillar, Fatehpur Sikri
items.description: Akbar's private audience hall centres on a single fantastical carved pillar from which the emperor is said to have presided over religious debate, a piece of architecture unlike anything else in India. It is the intellectual heart of Fatehpur Sikri and a highlight for the curious.

items.name: Buland Darwaza, Fatehpur Sikri
items.description: Among the tallest gateways in the world, Akbar's 'Gate of Magnificence' rises in a sweep of red sandstone and marble to commemorate his Gujarat victory. Climbing the great flight of steps to pass beneath it is one of the most theatrical arrivals in Mughal India.

items.name: Panch Mahal, Fatehpur Sikri
items.description: The five-storey open pavilion of ever-diminishing columned tiers, built for the ladies of the court to catch the breeze, is Fatehpur Sikri's most photographed and most playful structure. A perfect place to pause and imagine the vanished palace life.

items.name: Yamuna river view from the Taj plinth
items.description: From the rear terrace of the Taj, the Yamuna curves away past Mehtab Bagh and the far-bank tombs, a quieter vantage most visitors skip in the rush to the front facade. Lingering here at sunrise, with the river mist lifting, is where the Taj feels most private.

items.name: Taj Mahal calligraphy & inlay detail (interior)
items.description: Beyond the silhouette, the Taj's genius is in the detail, the perfectly proportioned Quranic calligraphy that appears the same size top to bottom, and the pietra-dura flowers set with dozens of stones per bloom. A specialist guide who reads these turns a photo-stop into an unforgettable close study of the craft.

items.name: Govardhan Hill parikrama
items.description: The sacred hill Krishna is said to have lifted draws pilgrims for the reverent circumambulation through Braj countryside dotted with kunds (tanks) and shrines. For a devout family it is among the most meaningful experiences of the region; the concierge can arrange a comfortable, well-paced version.

items.name: Gokul & Mahavan
items.description: The riverside village where Krishna was raised by Nanda and Yashoda is gentler and less crowded than the main temple towns, wrapped in pastoral Braj calm. A rewarding extension for pilgrims who want the whole Krishna story, not just its busiest chapters.

items.name: Nidhivan, Vrindavan
items.description: A dense, mysterious grove at the heart of Vrindavan's legends, where devotees believe Krishna and Radha still dance at night and no one may stay after dark. Steeped in myth and atmosphere, it is a quieter, stranger stop for those drawn to the mystical side of Braj.

items.name: Kusum Sarovar, Govardhan
items.description: A beautiful sandstone bathing tank ringed by steps and pavilions, luminous at sunset and blessedly serene, one of Braj's loveliest and least-visited spots. A photogenic, peaceful pause on a Mathura–Govardhan circuit.

items.name: Shopping for zardozi & marble at a trusted emporium
items.description: Agra's finest marble-inlay tables and boxes and its heavy zardozi embroidery deserve a vetted, no-pressure showroom rather than a tout on the street. The concierge's shortlist of reputable ateliers means genuine stones, honest pricing and reliable shipping home.

items.name: Sunset over the Taj from Agra Fort's Musamman Burj
items.description: From the octagonal marble tower where the imprisoned Shah Jahan spent his final years, the Taj floats on the horizon exactly as he last saw it, the single most poignant view in the city. Time a late-afternoon fort visit to end here as the light turns gold.

items.name: Cycle-rickshaw dawn safari, Keoladeo
items.description: The park bans motor vehicles on its inner tracks, so the classic way in is a licensed cycle-rickshaw whose driver doubles as a sharp-eyed guide, stopping silently for every heron and kingfisher. A gentle, low-effort wildlife morning that suits every generation of a family.

items.name: Radha Kund & Shyam Kund, Govardhan
items.description: The twin sacred tanks are among the holiest sites in Braj for followers of Radha-Krishna, quiet and intensely devotional away from the temple-town bustle. A meaningful stop for pilgrims completing the Braj circuit, best reached with a knowledgeable local escort.

items.name: Guru ka Taal
items.description: A historic stepped water reservoir turned Sikh gurudwara on the road out to Sikandra, its carved sandstone tank an atmospheric and little-known stop. An easy, quiet pause for those combining Akbar's Tomb with the drive toward Mathura.

items.name: Esphahan
credentials: Inside The Oberoi Amarvilas, the city's defining hotel
items.description: Recipes from the Mughal emperors' kitchens, served to live traditional music, the grandest table in Agra.

items.name: Peshawri
credentials: Inside ITC Mughal, a Luxury Collection Resort & Spa
items.description: North-West Frontier cooking from clay tandoors, the ITC signature, eaten family-style with your hands.

items.name: Dining at The Oberoi Amarvilas
credentials: Inside The Oberoi Amarvilas, the city's defining hotel
items.description: All-day international and Indian cooking framed by Taj views and Mughal gardens, faultless, and beautifully set.

items.name: Pinch of Spice
credentials: Featured by Condé Nast Traveller India
items.description: The city's best-loved standalone Mughlai kitchen, rich, well-balanced, and consistently good.

items.name: Mama Chicken Mama Franky House
credentials: Long-standing Agra street-food institution (Sadar Bazaar landmark)
items.description: An Agra street-food institution, decades of queues for its rolls, kebabs and franky.

items.name: The Bar at The Oberoi Amarvilas
credentials: Inside The Oberoi Amarvilas, the city's defining hotel
Rare uninterrupted Taj Mahal view from the bar
items.description: Uninterrupted Taj Mahal views framed in tall windows, the grandest, and quietest, nightcap in the city.

items.name: The Lounge, The Oberoi Amarvilas
credentials: Inside The Oberoi Amarvilas, the city's defining hotel
Terrace with Taj Mahal views, sunrise to nightfall
items.description: Golden-domed lounge and open-air terrace for high tea, sundowners and the play of light on the Taj.

plan.heading: 2 days in Agra, done well
plan.lede: A day-by-day shape for the trip, the pace we would set. Your advisor books the flights and the rooms; the days are yours.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: Enter the Taj Mahal at first light through the east gate with a historian, staying past the coach crowds as the marble warms.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: Rest at the Oberoi Amarvilas, whose every room faces the mausoleum, then tour Agra Fort in the softer afternoon light.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: Dinner at Esphahan at the Amarvilas, with live santoor and the Taj framed from the terrace.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: Drive to the abandoned red-sandstone capital of Fatehpur Sikri before the day heats, walking the Buland Darwaza and the Diwan-i-Khas.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: Return via the marble-inlay ateliers of the old craftsmen, or the quieter tomb of Itmad-ud-Daulah, the 'Baby Taj', across the Yamuna.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: A final Taj-facing dinner and an early night before onward travel.

items.name: Taj Ganj / East Gate
items.description: Closest to the monument with rooftop Taj views; best for the dawn visit without a long transfer.

items.name: Fatehabad Road
items.description: Where the larger luxury hotels sit; suits those wanting full-service comfort a short drive from the Taj.

items.name: Civil Lines
items.description: The older, greener administrative quarter; for a calmer, more local base.

events.name: Taj Mahotsav
events.note: A ten-day arts, crafts and cuisine festival near the Taj celebrating Mughal-era culture.

events.name: Full-moon night viewings
events.note: Limited-ticket night entry on five nights each lunar month, excluding Fridays and Ramadan.

events.name: Ram Barat
events.note: A vast, spectacular local wedding-procession festival unique to Agra, staged with great pageantry.

events.name: Diwali
events.note: The old city lights up; a fine time to pair the monuments with festive markets, though book early.

onGround.heading: On the ground
onGround.note: Go to the Taj at sunrise, the light is best and the crowds thinnest, and it is closed on Fridays. Stay in a room or hotel with a Taj view on the eastern side, and be ready to leave phones and large bags at security.

rows.label: Arriving
rows.value: Most arrive by a chauffeured car from Delhi (about three and a half hours on the Yamuna Expressway) or by the morning Gatimaan Express train; Agra's own airport has few flights, so the car is usually the discreet choice.

rows.label: Getting around
rows.value: A private car with driver between the monuments, then walk the last stretch, the Taj Mahal complex is car-free, so an electric buggy or a short walk covers the approach.

rows.label: Connectivity
rows.value: 4G and hotel wifi are dependable; a preloaded Jio or Airtel eSIM keeps you connected without a local SIM.

rows.label: Money
rows.value: Indian rupee (INR); hotels and monument tickets take cards, but carry cash for guides, buggies and small purchases, with a 10 percent tip customary.

rows.label: Climate
rows.value: November to February is the window: cool mornings, soft light on the marble, though December-January dawns can bring haze. Avoid May-June for the punishing heat and July-September for the monsoon.

rows.label: Flights from India
rows.value: No reliable scheduled service into Agra's small airport; the practised route is to fly into Delhi (from anywhere in India, plus international) and take the Gatimaan Express, about 1h40m, or drive the Yamuna Expressway in roughly 3-3.5 hours. Use the Delhi lounge before the onward train or car.

rows.label: Health & safety
rows.value: No special vaccinations; routine Hep A/typhoid cover advised. Safe for visitors, though the tourist crush around the Taj draws touts, so a private guide keeps it smooth. Sealed water only; air quality dips in winter.

rows.label: Dining, veg & Jain
rows.value: Wholly easy; the region is vegetarian-first and Jain requests are routine. Pinch of Spice and Esphahan at the Oberoi Amarvilas serve strong vegetarian menus; petha, the local sweet, is vegetarian.
